# stream-agents

> Local web viewer and usage API for AI coding-agent transcripts (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) on one machine. It reads the local transcript stores, renders sessions as HTML, and serves daily token and cost aggregates, active sessions and Claude subscription limits as JSON so other programs (dashboards, menu bars, other machines) can collect agent spend.

- Base URL: `http://<host>:7777` (the binary defaults to `127.0.0.1:7777`; `make run` / `make tray` listen on `0.0.0.0:7777`). `-listen` takes a comma-separated list of addresses.
- Auth: none. Everything is read-only (GET/HEAD); there is no CORS and no endpoint that writes or runs anything.
- Access: non-loopback peers reach only `/api/v1/*`, `/llms.txt` and `/llm.txt`. Every other path answers them `403 forbidden`, because it shows prompts and session content, unless the server runs with `-allow-remote-ui`. Loopback peers reach everything.
- This file is also served at `/llm.txt`.

## Network API (stable, for other programs)

Fields may be added; existing ones are never renamed or removed.

### GET /api/v1/health

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "version": "440b010e11d9",
  "host": "mac-mini"
}
```

`version` is the module version or VCS revision; `host` is the OS hostname.

### GET /api/v1/usage?days=N

Daily aggregates for the last `N` local calendar days including today, oldest first. `days` defaults to 31 and is capped at 400. One entry per agent and model per day; days without usage have `"by": []`.

```json
{
  "generated_at": "2026-11-02T09:27:39Z",
  "timezone": "Europe/Berlin",
  "utc_offset": "+01:00",
  "currency": "USD",
  "cost_multipliers": { "codex": 1.75 },
  "days": [
    {
      "date": "2026-11-01",
      "by": [
        {
          "agent": "codex",
          "provider": "openai",
          "model": "gpt-6-sol",
          "input_tokens": 26152,
          "output_tokens": 151,
          "cache_read_tokens": 17792,
          "cache_write_tokens": 0,
          "cost": 0.057372,
          "billed": 0.100402,
          "cost_partial": false,
          "sessions": 2
        }
      ]
    },
    { "date": "2026-11-02", "by": [] }
  ]
}
```

- `date`: local calendar day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) in `timezone`; `utc_offset` is the offset at `generated_at`.
- `agent`: `claude`, `codex` or `opencode`. `provider` is empty for agents that don't record one (Claude, Codex). `model` is empty when unknown.
- Tokens are raw token counts. `cost` is an estimate in USD at standard API prices (OpenCode's own stored cost when present). `billed` = `cost` × the agent's entry in `cost_multipliers` (unlisted agents are 1). Costs are rounded to 6 decimals.
- `cost_partial: true` means some tokens used a model with no known price, so `cost` is too low.
- `sessions`: sessions started that day that used this model. A session counts towards the local day it **started**, even if it ran past midnight.

### GET /api/v1/sessions

"Who needs me": the agent sessions on this machine that are working right now or waiting for the user. Cheap enough to poll every 2–3 s.

```json
{
  "generated_at": "2026-11-11T19:28:48Z",
  "host": "mac-mini",
  "sessions": [
    {
      "agent": "claude",
      "id": "91046aec-446f-43ec-844e-906a79f1154a",
      "project": "tradebot",
      "title": "Trading efficiency analysis",
      "model": "claude-fable-5-2",
      "state": "waiting",
      "waiting_reason": "turn_done",
      "since": "2026-11-11T16:44:18Z",
      "last_activity": "2026-11-11T16:44:54Z"
    },
    {
      "agent": "claude",
      "id": "fe0712e7-d288-4981-8c00-41731174a809",
      "project": "stream-agents",
      "title": "Stream-agents who-needs-me API",
      "model": "claude-opus-5-5",
      "state": "working",
      "waiting_reason": "",
      "since": "2026-11-11T19:17:18Z",
      "last_activity": "2026-11-11T19:28:44Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

- `sessions` is `[]` when nothing is active. Order: `waiting` first, longest waiting (oldest `since`) first; then `working`, most recent `last_activity` first.
- `agent`: `claude`, `codex` or `opencode`. `id` is the same ID as in `/session/{agent}/{id}`.
- `project`: last path element of the session's working directory. `title`: the same title the HTML UI shows (for Claude, Claude Code's own generated title when it wrote one, else the first prompt, cut to 120 characters); `""` if none. `model`: model of the latest reply (OpenCode: `provider/model`); `""` if unknown.
- `state`: `working` (a turn is in progress) or `waiting` (the agent is idle and the next move is the user's). `waiting_reason`: `turn_done` (the agent finished or the user interrupted it), `permission` (Claude Code is blocked on a permission prompt or an MCP input dialog; only reported when the optional `stream-agents hook` Claude Code hook is installed, see below), `""` while working.
- `since`: when the session entered `state`. `last_activity`: newest meaningful transcript record (or subagent write). Both RFC 3339 UTC.

How state is read (transcripts only, read-only):

- Claude Code: an assistant record with `stop_reason` `end_turn`/`stop_sequence`, a `turn_duration` system record, or an `[Request interrupted…]` user record ends the turn. A new prompt, a tool result or an assistant record that stopped for `tool_use` means working. Bookkeeping records (attachments, api-request, mode, ai-title, file-history, away summaries, compaction summaries, meta records, local slash commands such as `/model`) don't change the state.
- Codex: `task_started` / `user_message` events start a turn, `task_complete` / `turn_aborted` end it. Rollouts from Codex versions that write neither are reported `working` while active.
- OpenCode: the last message decides: a user message, an assistant message without `time.completed`, or one that finished with `tool-calls` is working; any other completed assistant message (`stop`, `length`, error, abort) ends the turn.

Permission prompts (Claude Code only, needs the hook from the README in `~/.claude/settings.json`): `stream-agents hook` records `PermissionRequest` and `Notification` (`permission_prompt`, `elicitation_dialog`, `elicitation_url_dialog`) events in `<state dir>/claude/<session>[.agent-<id>].json` and removes the file on `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `SubagentStop`, `SessionEnd` (tool events clear only the agent they fired in). The state dir defaults to `~/.local/state/stream-agents` (`-state-dir`, `STREAM_AGENTS_STATE_DIR`). A recorded prompt makes the session `waiting`/`permission` with `since` = when the prompt was recorded, until the transcript has a newer record (an answered or denied prompt is followed by a tool result) or the file is removed. Without the hook, a session blocked on a prompt reports `working`.

Which sessions are active:

- Not listed at all: subagent/sidechain transcripts (Claude `subagents/` and `isSidechain` files, OpenCode child sessions, Codex subagents), and runs driven by a program rather than a person: Claude `entrypoint` `sdk-*` (`claude -p`, Agent SDK), `codex exec`, and Codex sessions started by another client (e.g. the Codex plugin in Claude Code).
- A parent whose background subagent is still running is `working`: Claude subagent transcripts written after the parent's turn ended within the last 10 min and not marked `"finished": true` in their `.meta.json`; OpenCode child sessions that are working.
- Claude Code terminal sessions (`entrypoint` `cli`): Claude keeps a process registry in `<config dir>/sessions/<pid>.json`, each entry tagged with its pid namespace (`pidDomain`). Only entries in the server's own namespace are checked: if a live local process has the session open, it is listed in either state for up to 24 h after `last_activity` (a pid-reuse guard); if its local process is gone, or it has no entry while every registry entry is local, the session was closed and is dropped (a `working` session stays for 10 min, covering the moment before a process registers). Sessions whose entry is from another namespace (Claude running in a container or VM that shares the config dir) can't be checked and follow the windows below.
- Everything else (Codex, OpenCode, Claude without a usable registry entry): `working` is listed for 10 min after `last_activity` (the same window as `/hot.json`), `waiting` for 30 min. So a Codex or OpenCode session left waiting longer than 30 min disappears even if its window is still open.

### GET /api/v1/limits

Claude subscription usage limits (what Claude Code's `/usage` shows) for the account used on this machine. The server never calls Anthropic. It combines two local sources and uses whichever is newer for the 5-hour and weekly numbers:

1. **Status line (live)**: `stream-agents statusline` set as Claude Code's status line command (README) records the `rate_limits` Claude Code passes to the status line after each API response of a running session (a documented status-line field). Fresh to within seconds while any session on this machine is in use.
2. **Usage cache**: `cachedUsageUtilization` in Claude Code's `.claude.json`, which Claude Code only rewrites when it fetches usage itself, mainly when someone opens `/usage`. It can be hours or days old, but it is the only source of the per-model limits, `extra_usage` and `weekly_breakdown`.

Cheap (a few small file reads); polling every minute is fine.

```json
{
  "generated_at": "2026-11-11T22:14:44Z",
  "host": "mac-mini",
  "available": true,
  "origin": "statusline",
  "fetched_at": "2026-11-11T22:14:40Z",
  "age_seconds": 4,
  "statusline_at": "2026-11-11T22:14:40Z",
  "cache_fetched_at": "2026-11-11T19:10:32Z",
  "source": "~/.claude.json",
  "five_hour": { "percent": 31, "resets_at": "2026-11-12T00:14:40Z", "reset": false },
  "seven_day": { "percent": 13, "resets_at": "2026-11-18T20:00:00Z", "reset": false },
  "seven_day_opus": null,
  "seven_day_sonnet": null,
  "session": { "percent": 31, "resets_at": "2026-11-12T00:14:40Z", "reset": false },
  "limits": [
    { "kind": "session", "group": "session", "percent": 31, "severity": "normal", "resets_at": "2026-11-12T00:14:40Z", "reset": false, "is_active": false, "model": "", "surface": "" },
    { "kind": "weekly_all", "group": "weekly", "percent": 13, "severity": "normal", "resets_at": "2026-11-18T20:00:00Z", "reset": false, "is_active": false, "model": "", "surface": "" },
    { "kind": "weekly_scoped", "group": "weekly", "percent": 14, "severity": "normal", "resets_at": "2026-11-18T20:00:00Z", "reset": false, "is_active": true, "model": "Fable", "surface": "" }
  ],
  "extra_usage": { "enabled": false, "percent": null, "spend_limit_reached": false },
  "weekly_breakdown": [
    { "key": "claude_code", "name": "Claude Code", "percent": 94 },
    { "key": "chat", "name": "Chats", "percent": 5 },
    { "key": "cowork", "name": "Cowork", "percent": 1 },
    { "key": "other", "name": "Other", "percent": 0 }
  ]
}
```

- Always `200`, even with nothing to read: then `available: false`, `origin: ""`, every window, time and `extra_usage` `null`, `source` `""`, `limits` and `weekly_breakdown` `[]`. Every field is present in every response, `null` when unknown.
- `origin`: where `five_hour`, `seven_day`, `session` and the `session` / `weekly_all` entries of `limits` come from: `statusline` or `cache`. `fetched_at` is when those numbers were current; `age_seconds` = `generated_at` − `fetched_at`. `statusline_at` (last status line report on this machine) and `cache_fetched_at` (the cache's `fetchedAtMs`) are each source's own time, `null` if absent. Everything else (`seven_day_opus`, `seven_day_sonnet`, per-model `limits`, `extra_usage`, `weekly_breakdown`) always comes from the cache and is as old as `cache_fetched_at`.
- `percent`: 0–100 of the limit used (may be fractional, rounded to 2 decimals); `null` if unknown. `resets_at`: RFC 3339 UTC, `null` when no window is running (e.g. an idle 5-hour session). `reset: true` means `resets_at` was already past at `generated_at`: the window rolled over after the reading, so `percent` is from the previous window (show it as 0 / stale).
- `five_hour`, `seven_day`, `seven_day_opus`, `seven_day_sonnet`: utilization windows. `seven_day` is the weekly limit across all models. `session` is the 5-hour session limit (the `limits` entry of kind `session`); if either `session` or `five_hour` is missing it is copied from the other, and `seven_day` falls back to the `weekly_all` entry. The status line only reports `five_hour` and `seven_day`, and leaves out a window whose reset time has passed; a missing one keeps the cache's value.
- `limits`: Claude Code's own list, in its order. `kind`: `session`, `weekly_all`, `weekly_scoped` (a per-model weekly limit; `model` is its display name, e.g. `Fable`), possibly others. `group`: `session` / `weekly`. `severity`: `normal` or a warning level. `is_active`: the limit Claude Code currently considers binding.
- `extra_usage`: pay-as-you-go credits beyond the plan; `percent` is of the monthly credit limit.
- `weekly_breakdown`: share of this week's usage per surface (`claude_code`, `chat`, `cowork`, `other`); sums to ~100, not a limit.
- The limits are per account, not per machine: with several machines on one account, show the answer with the newest `fetched_at` instead of summing. A machine with no session in use (and nobody opening `/usage`) serves old numbers.
- Status line file: `<state dir>/limits.json` (state dir as for the hook: `-state-dir`, `STREAM_AGENTS_STATE_DIR`, default `~/.local/state/stream-agents`). An unchanged reading is rewritten at most every 30 s, so `statusline_at` can lag by that much while nothing changes. Claude Code only includes `rate_limits` for subscribers after a session's first API response. Sessions in a container only feed it if the container runs the same binary with a state dir shared with the host.
- Cache files: `.claude.json` in `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, next to the `-claude-dir` / `-claude-config-dir` projects dirs, `~/.claude.json` and `~/.claude*/.claude.json`; the one with the newest `fetchedAtMs` wins and is named in `source` (home dir shown as `~`). The account UUID in the cache is never exposed.
- **Undocumented source**: `cachedUsageUtilization` is Claude Code's internal cache, not a public API, and can change with any Claude Code release. Missing, renamed or mistyped keys come out as `null` / `""` / `false` / dropped list entries, never as an error. Treat every field as optional.

## Local-only endpoints (loopback, or `-allow-remote-ui`)

Used by the web UI and the menu bar; shapes may change.

### GET /api/summary.json

Totals for the menu bar: `today`, `week` (last 7 days incl. today), `month` (current calendar month), `lastMonth`, `last3Months` (current and two previous months), plus currently `active` sessions. Note the camelCase keys, unlike `/api/v1`.

```json
{
  "today": {"from":"2026-11-02","to":"2026-11-02","sessions":0,"tokens":0,"cost":0,"billed":0,"costPartial":false,"agents":[]},
  "week": {"from":"2026-10-27","to":"2026-11-02","sessions":3,"tokens":65481,"cost":0.1005364,"billed":0.1759387,"costPartial":false,
           "agents":[{"agent":"codex","sessions":3,"tokens":65481,"cost":0.1005364,"billed":0.1759387,"costPartial":false}]},
  "month": {"from":"2026-11-01","to":"2026-11-02","sessions":2,"tokens":44095,"cost":0.0573724,"billed":0.1004017,"costPartial":false,"agents":[]},
  "lastMonth": {"from":"2026-10-01","to":"2026-10-31","sessions":59,"tokens":4789071,"cost":5.1710876,"billed":9.0494033,"costPartial":false,"agents":[]},
  "last3Months": {"from":"2026-09-01","to":"2026-11-02","sessions":167,"tokens":115131561,"cost":114.443,"billed":197.102,"costPartial":false,"agents":[]},
  "active": [{"agent":"claude","title":"Fix the parser","url":"/session/claude/<id>"}]
}
```

`tokens` here is the sum of input, output and cache tokens. Costs are not rounded.

### GET /hot.json

Recently active sessions for the "Active" panel, as a JSON array (`[]` when none).

### HTML pages

- `GET /` — session list by project and modified time. Query: `agent`, `project`, `date`.
- `GET /session/{agent}/{id}` — one transcript rendered as HTML (`agent` is `claude`, `codex` or `opencode`).
- `GET /search?q=...&agent=...` — full-text search over transcripts.
- `GET /stats` — filterable year/month/day summaries, agent breakdown and activity heatmaps (groups by **UTC** day, unlike the API).
- `GET /assets/...` — static CSS/JS.

### Server-sent events

- `GET /stream/{agent}/{id}?offset=N` — `text/event-stream` of new transcript records from byte offset `N` (Claude and Codex only).
- `GET /notify` — `text/event-stream` that announces growth of recently active sessions; keepalive every 15 s.

## Errors

Plain-text bodies.

- `400` — bad query, e.g. `days must be a positive integer`.
- `403` — `forbidden`: a non-loopback peer asked for a local-only path.
- `404` — unknown path (including any unknown `/api/...`) or session.
- `405` — non-GET/HEAD on `/api/v1/*`; `Allow: GET, HEAD`.
- `500` — transcripts could not be listed (never from `/api/v1/limits`).

## Gotchas

- Costs are estimates from token counts and a small price table; they ignore historical price changes and fast/batch/regional/long-context modifiers. Unknown models have no cost. Usage that never reaches local transcripts (Codex memories, cloud tasks) is missing.
- `billed` defaults to a 1.75× multiplier for Codex only. Override with `-cost-multiplier codex=1,claude=1.2` or `STREAM_AGENTS_COST_MULTIPLIER`; listed agents replace the defaults.
- Days are computed in the server's time zone (`TZ` overrides it). `/api/v1/usage`, `/api/summary.json` and the `stats` CLI use local days; the HTML `/stats` page uses UTC days, so its numbers can differ near midnight.
- `/api/v1/usage` matches `stream-agents stats -group day -breakdown` for the same days.
- Each machine only sees its own transcripts: poll every machine and sum.
- Requests reuse an in-memory index; only transcripts that changed since the last request are re-read, so polling every minute is cheap (`/api/v1/sessions` every 2–3 s is fine: a poll is a directory scan plus a few `stat`s, ~20 ms). The first request after start builds the index and can take several seconds.
- `/api/v1/sessions`: a permission prompt can't be told apart from a running tool in a transcript, so without the hook a session blocked on one reports `working`; Codex and OpenCode prompts are never detected. A Claude session whose Stop hook is still running after the final reply already reports `waiting`. The process check only works for Claude processes in the server's own pid namespace (same machine, not in a container); sessions run in containers fall back to the 10/30 min windows, so one left waiting longer than 30 min disappears.
